title: Exact sparse-spectrum work budget
statement: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, define $B(n,k)$ as follows: if $n>0$, let $I$ be the exact sparse-spectrum Goldreich–Levin input with parameters $n$ and $k$, and set $B(n,k)$ equal to the sum of the rounding work for $I$ and the deterministic Goldreich–Levin work budget for $I$; if $n=0$, set $B(n,k)=1$.
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the exact sparse-spectrum input or the two work quantities, so their meanings cannot be made more explicit from the given context.
